correctness.rationale: Explicit finite-path binary shift dynamics imply F_t subset F_{t-d}; a second-block physical vertex witnesses every compatible residue intersection. Nerve theorem identifies the general path complex with translated cyclic motifs. For two holes the nerve is the Alexander dual of the independence complex of g disjoint cycles (K2 when L=2). The cycle suspension recurrence, joins, and integral Alexander duality yield the exact free homology rank and dimension. The packaged verifier independently checks 996 generic motif/period instances and 108 two-hole homology instances. Finite mod-2 verification is only corroboration.

originality.rationale: The arbitrary-binary-motif repeated-path-to-cycle homotopy transfer and its all-parameter two-hole path homology consequence were not stated or implied by the inspected primary avalanche-homology theorems or the closest indexed coprime-cycle result. Classical cycle-only cases are explicitly excluded from the novelty attribution. The new claim is a reduction for terminating repeated paths and a noncoprime two-hole family, not a restatement of the cyclic consecutive-support classification. Unindexed implicit coverage is an acknowledged residual risk.
residual_risks: A general repeated-path nerve reduction could be implicit in unindexed literature or within later versions of avalanche papers.

value.rationale: A general, finite-length stable homotopy reduction connects terminating directed-path binary avalanches to cyclic ones for every motif after two repetitions. The exact two-hole specialization yields motivated quantitative higher-dimensional topology, with ranks 2^g at lengths 3g and g>=2, and proves repeat-count independence. The result fills a natural multi-parameter gap in the initiating 2026 invariant, rather than merely computing a small special case.
